District - Ratlam (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 5(l)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 02/09/2024.

2. Heard the arguments.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
6. According to the material available on case diary, applicant Darshan enticed and kidnapped the minor victim aged around 17 years and 10 months and subjected her to penetrative sexual assault.
However, the victim deposed in her statement recorded under section 183 of the BNSS, 2023 that she had liking for the applicant for last five years.
They desired to marry.
As her parents were trying to marry her elsewhere, she insisted the applicant to take her along.
The applicant had physical relations with her consent.
There was no compulsion or enticement by the applicant.
The veracity of prosecution will be determined after evidence in the trial.
As informed, the applicant is aged around 18 years and is a labourer by profession.

7. Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20772 3 MCRC-30028-2025 fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio economic status of the applicants, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.

However, the observations,
herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

8. Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicants on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
